No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. git fetch origin 6798c505a6b81cbafc7d43b98fedba141d59680b && git checkout 6798c505a6b81cbafc7d43b98fedba141d59680b

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fb3c2cc478f49ad9d6fa6322f411dcefe4ee56c8`

Scope: `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/dev-seed-credential-retirement.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/forced-reset-revocation.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/dev-seed-credential-retirement.test.ts`, `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts/plugins/plugin-auth.md`, `.changeset/35184-dev-seed-retire-at-boot.md`, `.changeset/dev-seed-credential-production-refusal.md`, `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx` + cited, read only: `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/dev-seed-credential.ts`, `operator-password-reset.ts`, `credential-change-ends-reset-tokens.ts`, `password-reset-ends-added-access.ts`, `admin-user-endpoints.ts`, `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts`, `auth-manager.ts`, `session-tombstone.ts`, `index.ts`, `package.json` (same package), `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts`, `sys-session.object.ts`, `sys-api-key.object.ts`, `packages/core/src/kernel.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/user/set-password.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migration-plugins.ts`, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/execution-duties.md`, `contract-review.md`, `landing-operations.md`

Head note. This record is for `fb3c2cc478`. Merge base: `115d38788e`. Eight files, 840 insertions, 18 deletions. Everything below is read from the diff, the tree and the check runs. Nothing was run.

### ① Derived judgments

**A boot outside development mode retires them: yes.** `AuthPlugin.start()` registers one `kernel:ready` hook that calls `retireDevSeedCredentials`. The function returns at once when `NODE_ENV` is `development`. Otherwise it reads the stamped accounts, keeps those whose seed credential is still in force (`isDevSeedCredentialInForce`), and for each runs the revocation the operator's reset runs (`revokeSessionsAndApiKeys`), ends the outstanding password-reset tokens, and ends the sessions a host `secondaryStorage` holds. The retirement also covers every session the seed account holds or opened, under the same fail-closed rule.

**A boot in development mode leaves them alone: yes.** The first line of the function. Pinned (case 2).

**Accounts without the stamp are unaffected: yes.** The only account list is the read on the stamp column. No other account id enters the loop. Pinned with an administrator-created control account in cases 1, 4 and 6.

**An operator-set credential is untouched: yes.** An account whose password changed since the seed fails the in-force check and is skipped, with everything it was issued later. Pinned (case 3) for the operator's reset and for an administrator's password write.

**A retired credential answers as a revoked one: yes.** Sessions are tombstoned in place in the shape the existing revocation writes. Keys get `revoked: true`. Case 1 reads the session through `/get-session` and the key through the key-admission seam (`API_KEY_REVOKED`).

**Before the first request: yes.** `kernel.ts` awaits `kernel:ready` and only then triggers `kernel:listening`. A handler that throws fails the boot. Case 5 pins the failed boot.

**The remedy command does not trip the retirement.** The hook is registered in `start()`. The CLI composes a stack's `AuthPlugin` for its declarations only (`start()` suppressed), so `os user set-password` does not run it.

**No more than the card: yes, with one remark.** The card says "sessions, API keys and tokens". The code also unlinks linked sign-in accounts, disables the OAuth applications the account registered and revokes the SCIM credentials it minted. That is the shared revocation `os user set-password` already performs, reused whole. The changeset and the docs list each item. I accept it as the card's rule ("nothing the development seed issued keeps acting"), see N4.

**Clause-② line: `no (narrowing)` is true.** The question is whether the card widens the accepted set or enlarges the public surface (`execution-duties.md` line 76). It does neither. `isLiveSession` gains `export` inside its module, but `src/index.ts` does not re-export `forced-reset-revocation.ts` or the new module, and `package.json` `exports` does not address them. So no public export is added. A card that narrows the accepted set is `Clause-②: no` (line 108). The PR body and the changeset carry the same line.

**Metadata-protocol line: `none` is true.** No key, accepted value or metadata type moves.

**DELIBERATE CORRECTION of `.changeset/dev-seed-credential-production-refusal.md`.** One physical line changed, in two places. The frontmatter and every other line are unchanged.

Place 1, the bold label.
OLD: "**Not ended at boot:**"
NEW: "**Ended by `os user set-password`, and at boot:**"
Correct. With this PR the boot ends them, so the old label would publish a false statement.

Place 2, the last sentence.
OLD: "Ending them at boot is follow-up #35184."
NEW: "In the same release, a boot outside development mode also retires them: see the note "a boot outside development mode retires what the development seed issued" (#36699)."
Correct. The quoted title is the title of the new changeset, character for character. #36699 is this PR. The sentence between the two places is unchanged and still true.

Not consumed: the file is on `origin/main` with the OLD text. No `CHANGELOG.md` and no release page on `origin/main` carries its text. The version PR #35129 (`changeset-release/main`) is open and unmerged. So the pending changeset is the right place to correct. "In the same release" holds as long as this PR lands before #35129 is cut (N6). **This correction is intended and correct.** `check-empty-changeset` is red on it by design. This same-head record at the contract-review tier is the confirmation `landing-operations.md` asks for.

### ② Semver level

- The new changeset grades `@objectstack/plugin-auth` `patch`. It is the only package whose published source moves. No `major`.
- `patch` is right. `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, breaking or not.
- The title's `!` is right for a narrowing. The changeset carries the **BREAKING** banner, FROM and TO, a one-line fix, and one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`).
- The corrected changeset keeps its levels.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The narrowing face.** Previously accepted, now refused: on a server outside development mode, a session, an API key, an authorized app, a device sign-in, a reset link or a linked sign-in of a seeded account still on its seed password. A second face: a boot that used to succeed now fails when the retirement cannot complete. The changeset states both. FROM: such a credential "kept working ... until an operator ran `os user set-password`". TO: the boot retires them; a session's next request is unauthenticated, a key is refused `403 API_KEY_REVOKED`; "When the retirement cannot complete, the boot fails with an error naming the accounts". The fix is one line: set each seeded account's password with `os user set-password <email>` before serving.
- **Fail closed: yes, by reading.** A failed in-force read, an incomplete revocation, a failed read or write in the added session arm, a failed reset-token end and a failed or unverifiable `secondaryStorage` end each add a reason. Any reason throws after the loop with the accounts and the remedy. A failed read of the stamped list and a failed auth-context read throw their own error, so the boot still fails, without the remedy sentence (N3). Two declared exceptions read as "no stamped account": an engine with no read surface, and a user table that was never created. Both match the existing refusals in `dev-seed-credential.ts`.
- **Idempotent: yes.** A retired account cannot open a session before the next boot. Case 4 pins equal tombstones over two boots and zero counts on a third pass.
- **Pins fail without the fix: consistent by reading.** Case 1 without the hook: the seed sessions resolve and the keys are admitted, so the `RETIRED` comparison is red. Case 1 without the hardening call: the added assertion is red (the PR body reports that red at `035b1fdfe`). Case 4: the direct call would count ended rows, red. Case 5: the boot would succeed, red. Case 6: the two seed sessions would resolve, red. Cases 2 and 3 are controls and stay green, as they should. The composition is real: `ObjectKernel`, ObjectQL on a SQLite file, `AuthPlugin`, `SecurityPlugin`, two boots over one file.
- **No test weakened.** The test file is new. No existing test changes.
- **Boot cost.** A database with no stamped account pays one read on `sys_user.dev_seed_credential`, which is indexed (`sys-user.object.ts` line 1696). A stamped account no longer in force pays its in-force reads at every boot, for as long as it carries the stamp. An account still in force pays the full revocation reads, sequentially, before the socket opens. One of those reads filters `sys_session` on a column with no index (N1).
- **SQL pushdown.** The stamped ids are read and then checked one by one. The in-force check compares a digest computed in the application, so it cannot be pushed down, and the list is the seed's few accounts. No finding.
- **Author.** PR `user.login` is `os-warren`, not the fleet bot. Read before landing.
- **A security item is with the owner seat.** It does not change this verdict.

### ④ Design judgment

The change does what card #35184 asks. One function, one hook, the operator's own revocation reused, and the same development-mode predicate the refusals use. Retiring only accounts whose seed credential is still in force is the right reading of "an operator-set credential is untouched": retiring on the bare stamp would end operator-era credentials at every restart. Failing the boot is the right failure for a rule that says nothing keeps acting.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Notes:
- N1. One read in the retirement filters `sys_session` on a column with no index and filters live rows in the application. Only an account still in force pays it, once per boot. Small today. An index, or a live-row predicate in the query, would be a follow-up, not this PR.
- N2. Fail-closed is pinned through one arm (a refused key write). The other arms (the in-force read, the added session arm, the `secondaryStorage` read-back) are fail-closed by reading and have no pin.
- N3. A failed read of the stamped list, or of better-auth's context, fails the boot with the raw error. It names no account and no remedy. The sentence in the changeset ("an error naming the accounts") holds for the per-account failures only.
- N4. While an account stays on its seed password, every boot retires again. A key or an OAuth application that a platform administrator restored is retired again at the next boot. The changeset says "only a platform administrator restores such a key" and does not say that. One clause in the changeset or the docs would make it complete. Prose face.
- N5. Linked sign-in accounts are deleted, though the header notes that a sign-in link "only opens a session, which `session.create.before` refuses". The same holds for a linked account. The end state equals the operator's reset, so I accept it. It is worth one line in the module header.
- N6. The corrected sentence says "In the same release". That needs this PR to land before version PR #35129 is cut. The PR body already lists the file overlap with #35129. If #35129 lands first, the corrected file is gone and the correction is moot.
- N7. CI at this head: `Check Changeset` is red by design. `PR-body guards` is also red, and not by design: it says #35184 is claimed by #36311. #36311 is now closed, so a re-run should clear it. The seat reads it green before landing.
- N8. The title's `!` owes the dogfood battery. The PR body says it was not run locally on the new commit. CI's `Dogfood Regression Gate` is green at this head.
- N9. The PR body declares the test file at about 11.4 s, over the 10 s file line, and gives its reason. This is the seat's L1 line.
- N10. The retirement's `rowsOf` reads an array or `{ value }`. The shared revocation's also reads `{ records }`. The engine returns arrays, so nothing breaks today. One shared helper would stop the two drifting.
